source_text:
Contra Severum Antiochenum (fragmentum ap. Pseudo-Anastasium
Sinaitam, Contra monophysitas)
89.1189 Ὀλυμπιοδώρου τοῦ μεγάλου φιλοσόφου διακόνου Ἀλεξανδρείας, ἐκ τοῦ
δευτέρου λόγου τοῦ κατὰ Σεβήρου, ἐν ᾧ παραγαγὼν τὴν χρῆσιν τοῦ ἁγίου
Ἀθανασίου τὴν λέγουσαν τὰ δύο θελήματα ἐπὶ Χριστοῦ, οὕτω πως διεξέρχεται
λέγων·
orientation: This is the introductory lemma that identifies the author, work, and the Athanasian quotation about two wills in Christ that Olympiodorus is about to expound.
pass_a_gloss: Of Olympiodorus the great philosopher, deacon of Alexandria, from the second book of the work against Severus, in which, having brought forward the quotation of Saint Athanasius that says the two wills in Christ, Olympiodorus goes through it in some such way, saying:

choices.why: The glossary mandates 'book' for λόγος when it refers to a division of a multi-part work, as here with 'second book'.
The glossary mandates 'quotation' for χρῆσις in the sense of a cited passage from an authority.
The glossary mandates 'wills' for θελήματα, specifically the two wills in Christ.
Renders the aorist participle's temporal/causal force in introducing the quotation.
Captures the sense of detailed exposition implied by the compound verb, matching the lemma's report that he 'expounded' it.

pass_b_english: From the second book of Olympiodorus, the great philosopher and deacon of Alexandria, against Severus. In it, after bringing forward the quotation from Saint Athanasius that speaks of two wills in Christ, Olympiodorus expounds it in this way, saying:

last_rejected.source_quote: Ὀλυμπιοδώρου τοῦ μεγάλου φιλοσόφου διακόνου Ἀλεξανδρείας
last_rejected.why: English omits 'deacon of Alexandria' from Olympiodorus's title.
last_rejected.fix: From the second book of Olympiodorus, the great philosopher and deacon of Alexandria, against Severus.
last_rejected.ruling: English includes 'deacon of Alexandria'; no omission. 'διακόνου Ἀλεξανδρείας' is present in the translation.
